title: と (and; with)
meaning: "and" (exhaustive list of nouns), "with (a person)", also marks quoted speech.
simpleExplanation: と has two everyday jobs. (1) "and" between nouns: パンと卵 "bread and eggs". This is a complete list; you are naming everything. (2) "with" a person: 友達と映画を見ます "I watch a film with a friend". と only ever connects nouns; to join verbs or adjectives you need the て-form instead.
whenUsed: Listing exactly the items you mean (shopping lists, family members, two places); saying who you do something with (friends, family, colleagues); and, later, quoting words with 言う and 思う.
formation: Person + と + verb  (友達と行きます)
Person + と + 一緒に + verb  (母と一緒に食べます)

rows.label: Example
cells: パンと卵を買いました
パンや卵を買いました

rows.label: Meaning
cells: I bought bread and eggs (that's all)
I bought things like bread and eggs

examples.ja: パンと卵を買いました。
examples.reading: パンと たまごを かいました。
examples.note: "and" between two nouns: a complete list.

examples.reading: ともだちと えいがを みます。
examples.en: I watch a film with a friend.

examples.ja: 母と電話で話しました。
examples.reading: ははと でんわで はなしました。
examples.en: I talked with my mother on the phone.
examples.note: "with" a person, plus で for the means (phone).

examples.ja: 家族と日本へ来ました。
examples.reading: かぞくと にほんへ きました。
examples.en: I came to Japan with my family.
examples.note: The person you do something with takes と.

examples.ja: スーパーで肉と野菜を買いました。
examples.reading: スーパーで にくと やさいを かいました。
examples.en: I bought meat and vegetables at the supermarket.
examples.note: The whole list 肉と野菜 is one object; を goes after the last noun only.

similarGrammar.difference: や = "and, among others" (an incomplete list). と names everything.
で = by means of a thing (バスで); と = together with a person (友達と).
To say "and" between verbs or adjectives (eat and drink; cheap and good), use the て-form, never と.

commonMistakes.why: と joins nouns only. Verbs are joined with the て-form.
Adjectives cannot be joined with と; use the て-form 安くて.

commonMistakes.wrong: パンを卵を買いました。
commonMistakes.right: パンと卵を買いました。
commonMistakes.why: Nouns in one list are joined with と; the object marker を comes once, at the end.

usageNotes: と joins nouns only — never verbs or adjectives (use て-form for those). と lists everything; や lists examples.
jlptTips: If the blank sits between two nouns and the options are と / や / も / の, ask: is it a complete list (と) or just examples with など nearby (や)?
If the noun before the blank is a person and the verb is an activity (行く, 話す, 遊ぶ), the answer is と ("with"), not で.
